To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a novel hESC‐derived HD neuronal culture model that exhibits mHTT aggregates, neurodegeneration, and a relationship between neurodegeneration and soluble mHTTexon1.

we developed a novel hESC‐derived HD neuronal line, which exhibits mHTT aggregates, neurodegeneration, and a quantitative relationship between soluble mHTT and neurodegeneration, thereby complementing existing HD neuronal models.

we have established a novel HD neuronal model from an isogenic hESC line that recapitulates disease‐relevant phenotypic features and exhibits a quantitative relationship between soluble monomeric mHTT levels and toxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing human embryonic stem cells (hESC) derived neuronal models of HD.
the development of a novel human embryonic cell‐derived Huntington’s disease (HD) neuronal model that exhibits disease‐relevant phenotypic features and is useful for studying HD pathogenesis.
the development of a new HD neuronal model that addresses the limitations of existing models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hESC‐based neuronal models provide a powerful tool for HD research, which complements the existing iPS‐based neuronal models.
the hESC‐HD model provides a robust and reproducible platform to study the molecular mechanisms and therapeutic targets for HD, which will be a valuable tool to accelerate HD research.
hESCs‐derived neuronal models expressing HT‐Texons1 are an excellent complement to iPSC‐derived neuronal models for HD research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hESC‐derived HD neuronal models are a powerful tool for HD research.
we have generated human embryonic stem (hESC) lines that can be differentiated into neurons and exhibit mHTT aggregation.
we have established a novel HD model derived from human embryonic stem cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have generated an isogenic HD neuronal model from hESCs, and this model recapitulates the key features of the disease, including mHTT aggregation and neurodegeneration, and that the level of soluble monomeric mHTT is the key factor that drives the neurodegeneration in our model.
the hESC‐based HD models provide valuable tools for studying the mechanisms of neurodegeneration and testing the therapeutic efficacy of drugs and gene therapy.
the hESCs‐derived neuronal model is an important tool for HD research and drug discovery.
